reviews_5s: Our family enjoys making cheeses and yogurt, as well as canning in the fall. When we make paneer, for example, we have used cheesecloth and our bare hands to squeeze the fluid out of the cheese, and I have, on more than occasion, burnt my hands trying to get all the liquid squeeze out. Knowing we can place the cheese into this strainer, while holding the handle and letting gravity help with some of it, sound ideal! Straining grape juice is another task that I think this new mesh strainer will tackle quickly and easily, freeing out hands to do other tasks at the same time. I have to be honest, though. I had to look up a video to see how to attach the cheese cloth to the rim. You have to unhook the zipper completely before reattaching it to the metal frame. There is a video on the product page that will help you, if you need to see a visual example. Once you completely unhook the zipper (imagine unzipping a jacket, and separating the two sides so they hang independently), you can then reattach to the frame. I think this item is a great tool to have on hand for tasks requiring cheesecloth. This cloth is much more tightly woven than I am used to, but I am thinking it will be ideal for the above tasks, as well as new ones we may encounter. i also appreciate that the cheese cloth bags are washable!I'm impressed with how well this worked, and the fabric and frame are very strong. A strong zipper holds the fabric bag securely to the frame. I made cream cheese. I left my curds to drain overnight in the refrigerator and all the liquid drained out. I didn't have to squeeze it, but you could if you wanted to hurry things along. What was really awesome was the curds slid right off the fabric. No sticking! The size is a little awkward--the bag is very long. It's approx. 5 inches wide but nearly a foot long. I wanted to collect all the whey so had to hang it in a tall pitcher to drain, and empty the pitcher a couple times because the bag almost reached the bottom of the pitcher. The fabric is extremely tight mesh so no small particles can get through.This strainer is an improvement over other similar looking ones, having a thicker metal handle that provides better stability when filtering nut milk. Despite the upgrade, the handle is still quite lightweight since it’s hollow, plus the point where it meets the ring frame doesn’t look to be very well attached. I was hoping for a solid steel rod for a handle to give it better balance. Regardless, the fine mesh bag does a fantastic job straining nut milk and catches the majority of the tiny crushed nut pulp. The zippered cloth bag is a clever design, allowing for easy removal and washing.I make a few things where I need a fine quality cloth strainer. I have some cheese cloth but even then that can let some sediment flow through that I need to keep out of certain liquids. This is very fine cloth and it is very sturdy. The frame and handle are very sturdy as well. The mesh bags easily unzip and zip up around the frame. I like that you can remove and wash if needed. Great addition to my kitchen.Needed something to strain custard for homemade ice cream and this did the trick. The bag was easy enough to clean and it comes with three so you have spares.
